context:
Goal: merges get faster and easier because lanes stay close to main.
Problem (rule): no rule or hook says when a lane brings main into its branch, and most open PRs are far behind. Each time a lane brings main in, it pushes, so its checks and review run again; that costs runs, time and tokens. It needs your word because it sets how often every lane pushes.
Based on (measured): the coordinator's REST read at 13:43 CST, main at 4680473b0, first 300 open PRs (a fourth page not read): 8 at main, 5 are 6 to 50 commits behind, 287 are more than 50 behind. Ready ones: #3553 at main, #3577 354 behind, #2917 394, #3548 482, #3097 1,710 (why #3097 is ready that far behind: unknown). Relayed; triage did not re-read it.
Based on (read): the four lanes the coordinator told brought main in within minutes, so it is easy to do; the cost is the re-run, not the effort.
Departs from: main — no rule says when a lane merges main in; a lane does it when it chooses, which today is right before lint and record. The options set a time.
Meanwhile: the coordinator acts on your pick, not before; nothing waits on this answer.

lastAnswer.note: typed in the coordinator's chat at 13:46 CST (relayed): probably this and/or PRs of a certain priority grade are all brought to main at once

options.gain: The fewest re-runs, so the least cost in runs, time and tokens.
options.how: A lane brings main in once, right before its lane lint and review record, and not again unless the merge tool says it is behind.
options.label: Only right before lint and record (today's habit, written down)
options.lose: Most open PRs stay far behind main, and a late catch-up can bring a big conflict at the end.

options.gain: Every lane stays at main, so a merge is a small step and conflicts show early.
options.how: Each lane brings main in after every merge to main.
options.label: Every live lane, after each merge to main
options.lose: Every live lane re-runs its checks and review after each merge to main, which costs many more runs, time and tokens.

options.gain: The lanes about to merge stay close to main for a few extra re-runs.
options.how: A lane that is ready, or one step from ready, brings main in; the others stay put until they near ready.
options.label: Only lanes marked ready or one step from it
options.lose: Lanes still in work fall behind, and a long-lived lane can drift far before it is ready.

ref: your question in the coordinator's chat, 13:39 CST Nov 16 ("how come lanes/checkouts are still not moving up to main when they are able to easily be fast forwarding their checkouts in their builds"); coordinator's measure, relayed at 13:45 CST
reply: Option c, closed at 13:48 CST Nov 16, from your words typed in the coordinator's chat at 13:46 CST (relayed): only lanes that are ready or one step from it bring main in after each merge. "One step from ready" is read as: lane lint PASS and the review record posted at the live head, not yet marked ready; tell me if you meant something else. The coordinator acts on it now. Your extra idea (PRs brought to main together by priority grade) was a hedge, not a pick: it is the new question below this one, with what grades exist today. Filed as ruling own-923-c-ready-lanes-bring-main-in; the rule's written home is step rewrite-merge-decisions-for-lane-merge.

shown.label: Only right before lint and record (today's habit, written down)
Every live lane, after each merge to main
Only lanes marked ready or one step from it

title: When should a lane bring main into its own branch: only before lint, after every merge to main, or only when it is ready or close to it?
why: The coordinator recommends c: it keeps the lanes about to merge close to main without a re-run on every lane after each merge. It is the coordinator's recommendation, not owner-typed.
